summary.suggested: The St. Louis Post-Dispatch reported that Tom Allen's bell rang and glasses smashed when the new manager of the Champion's Rest planned linoleum and new mirrors, so the sawdust and old fixtures were kept.

facts.fact: Allen named his saloon "Champion's Rest" thinking of the rest for his old age it was to be; it stood among the Market Street saloons between Sixth and Tenth streets
places: Champion's Rest, Market Street, St. Louis

facts.fact: Hartgrove took possession of the Champion's Rest under a document said to be Allen's will, leaving his daughter out; the daughter brought proceedings to dispossess her before Allen was buried, but the court probated the will and a manager, a former bartender of Allen's, was put in
places: Champion's Rest, Market Street, St. Louis

facts.fact: In Allen's time the saloon's doors were never locked, sawdust covered the floor, and "Weary Willies" bunked under the piano
places: Champion's Rest, Market Street, St. Louis

facts.fact: After Allen's death, a bell behind the bar that only Allen had used rang by itself and glasses broke when the new manager planned linoleum and new mirrors; the changes were dropped and Market Street believed it was Allen's spirit
places: Champion's Rest, Market Street, St. Louis
